citation: Jung, W. (2026), BuildOcc: A large language model occupant agent platform for building energy research, SoftwareX, 103068
description: BuildOcc provides occupant agents driven by large language models for building energy simulation, grounded in American Time Use Survey microdata. It was developed by Wooyoung Jung at the University of Arizona and described in SoftwareX (2026); version 1.0.1 was archived on Zenodo on 2 September 2026. Agents schedule activities from the time use survey across four demographic groups, receive personas with appliance ownership priors from the EIA Residential Energy Consumption Survey, keep a memory stream in the style of Park and colleagues (2023), respond to a typology of demand-response signals, and are checked by two tiers of behavioural and energy validation metrics. Coverage: United States households, as represented in the survey data. Access: a Python agent library, a REST API and a Model Context Protocol server, from GitHub and Zenodo. Licence: Apache 2.0; free, though running agents needs access to a language model. Caveats: language-model behaviour is stochastic and depends on the model used; validation is against aggregate survey statistics. Simulation uses are occupant behaviour and demand-response studies in building energy models and household load scenarios. Related records: EnergyPlus and other occupant behaviour models.
